assessment.nobel_worthiness: A compelling body of evidence and framework linking trade, technology, tasks, local labour markets, and distributional change.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are closely associated with the central empirical and conceptual advances represented here.
assessment.maturity: The work has reshaped labour, trade, and public-policy research over many years.
uncertainties: The broad programme spans several mechanisms and a Nobel citation would need to delimit its core contribution precisely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative evidence transformed the measurement and analysis of intergenerational mobility and place-based opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman have central, identifiable roles in the linked data infrastructure and empirical research programme.
assessment.maturity: Its findings, methods, and public-economics influence are well established, with extensive subsequent research.
uncertainties: The contribution combines data construction, measurement, and causal interpretation, whose respective boundaries require careful citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination directly measurable in consequential labour-market settings and changed empirical practice.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are strongly identified with landmark correspondence-study evidence in this programme.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, extended across markets and countries, and has enduring scientific influence.
uncertainties: The method and substantive evidence have a wider intellectual lineage than the listed candidate grouping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power has materially revised how economists understand wage setting and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning has a particularly clear foundational claim for synthesizing and advancing the monopsony framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large empirical literature and has become central to contemporary labour economics.
uncertainties: Empirical estimates and the scope of monopsony vary substantially across labour markets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life shocks, health, and skill formation established the long economic consequences of childhood conditions.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha each have prominent and complementary contributions to the empirical and dynamic human-capital literature.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated across settings and is influential in health, education, and public economics.
uncertainties: The umbrella includes distinct causal designs and theoretical mechanisms rather than one sharply bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collective household models replaced the unitary-family benchmark with a testable account of bargaining, allocation, and policy incidence.
assessment.attribution: Chiappori and Lundberg are central to the theoretical and empirical development of this research programme.
assessment.maturity: The approach is long established and has changed research in family, labour, and development economics.
uncertainties: The empirical applicability of collective-model restrictions and bargaining interpretations remains context dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion supplied durable behavioural foundations for economic interaction.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt are especially closely associated with the influential experimental and formal account of inequity aversion.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively tested and incorporated into organizational, labour, and behavioural economics.
uncertainties: Social-preference parameters and mechanisms are heterogeneous across contexts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run distributional accounts and new wealth data have substantially changed research on inequality, taxation, and capital ownership.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez, and Zucman are highly visible central contributors to the data, measurement, and analysis in this programme.
assessment.maturity: The research has sustained a major academic literature and broadened the empirical basis for studying inequality.
uncertainties: Data coverage, wealth valuation, and offshore-wealth measurement remain challenging and consequential.
